title: A Terminal for the Protocol
premise: Cyrus Marchetti has spent eleven years as the sole keeper of Beacon 7, an insurance relay orbiting a dying star, cataloging impossible accidents and staying deliberately off every registry. When the freighter Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children, Cyrus realizes her beacon is the only receiver that caught their distress signal—and that someone at the corporate core wants both ship and witness erased. Fleeing toward the relay at the edge of dead space, she must choose between transmitting the truth that will destroy the company she secretly serves and protecting Elian, the one crew member who aged forward instead, carrying memories of a future the protocol was built to prevent. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts everything, sacrificing her invisibility and nearly her life, and the last transmission is her own confession: she commissioned the beacon herself, decades ago, from a future she no longer remembers.
about_author: Wren Kavanagh is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years maintaining automated stations along the Arctic shipping lanes before turning to fiction. Their novels explore loneliness at the edge of infrastructure, where machines outlive their purposes and people outlive their alibis.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Routine aboard Beacon 7 shatters when the Halcyon docks unbidden, its crew of forty reduced to toddlers, except one man, Elian, who is older than the voyage should have made him. Cyrus hides the ship's transponder before company drones arrive, an instinct she can't explain. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness—she recognizes Elian's face from dreams she's never admitted having.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. The two flee in the beacon's ancient tender toward the edge relay, pursued by a 'salvage' vessel flying no colors. Elian reveals fragments: the crew volunteered for a time-dilation trial, and the protocol that reversed them was authored by someone named Marchetti. Emotional beat: wary intimacy—two strangers discovering they may have loved each other across an erased timeline.

chapters.title: Signal to Noise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the dead-space relay, they find it already occupied by a company auditor who offers Cyrus amnesty for silence—and shows her footage proving she signed the beacon's commission order in handwriting she doesn't recognize as her own. The salvage ship closes in; the relay's transmitter needs a human hand on the coupling, which means someone must stay behind. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: A Terminal for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. While Elian pilots the children to safety through the debris field, Cyrus holds the coupling open and broadcasts the full record—the reversed crew, the trial, her own signature from a future self. The salvage ship's fire tears through the relay, but the signal escapes. Rescued half-alive by Elian, she remembers nothing new, yet finally understands what she paid. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom.
